I have worked in a sliced cheese and shredded cheese factory.

They make shredded cheese by cutting a 600 pound block of cheese into smaller blocks then shredding it.

Sliced cheese, however, is they take the 600 pound block and melt it down sometimes adding salt or other stuff the customer wants in there and running the melted cheese over a ten foot wide cooling wheel. Then it gets cut into ribbons which then is sliced into the sliced cheese squares.

So shredded cheese is not processed at all from the original block but sliced cheese is.

It's a texture issue and more likely a type issue.

FIRST:

You don't just taste your foods, chemically, with your tastebuds... you also taste via textures and consistency. There's an experiment we used to do with hotdogs, in elementary school, that you can try to prove this: boil a few hotdogs, and put one on a plate, and put another in a food processor and puree it into a fine paste. Take a bite of the regular hotdog (no bun or condiments) and note how it tastes. Then take a little of the hotdog-paste, and note how that tastes (spoiler, it's pretty nasty). Nothing has changed about the hotdog, other than its texture and consistency, but they taste different.

I'm assuming that this is the same for cheese.

SECOND:

Are you talking about the same type of cheese? Most people attribute sliced cheese as American cheese, and usually the Kraft kind. But shredded cheese is usually a cheddar, Mexican blend, mozzarella, or another higher quality type of cheese. Unless you're comparing sliced and shredded variants of the same cheeses, you're not going to have a very valid comparison.
